entities.summary: Olgus was a 2nd-century economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in the Roman Empire. He made significant contributions to the understanding of monarchs and rulers, which influenced the development of political theory and governance in the region. Olgus' work has been rediscovered in recent years, shedding new light on the social and economic dynamics of the ancient world. His ideas continue to resonate with scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complexities of power and authority in the ancient Roman state. As a testament to his lasting impact, Olgus' writings have been translated into multiple languages and remain a staple of scholarly research in the field.
